title: Asynchronous JavaScript Multiple Choice
description: Event loop, microtasks vs macrotasks, promises, async/await, and error handling from module 03.

questions.explanation: Synchronous code on the call stack always runs first, even before a `setTimeout(0)` callback. The timer callback goes into the task queue and only runs after the current script finishes.
Sync code runs first (`start`, `end`). The event loop then drains the entire microtask queue (promise reactions) before running the next macrotask, so `micro` prints before `macro`.

questions.prompt: What does calling an `async function` always return, even if it has no `await` inside?
questions.explanation: Every `async function` wraps its return value in a `Promise`. Even `async function f() { return 1; }` returns a promise that resolves to `1`, not `1` directly.

questions.prompt: When an `async function` hits an `await`, what happens?

options.text: The entire JavaScript engine blocks until the awaited promise settles
The function pauses and yields control; the rest of the function resumes as a microtask once the promise settles
The function immediately throws if the promise has not settled yet
`await` has no effect unless used inside a `for` loop

questions.explanation: `await` pauses only the current async function; the rest of the program keeps running. When the promise settles, the continuation is scheduled as a microtask, not a blocking operation.

options.text: An unhandled rejection crashes the process

questions.explanation: `try`/`catch` around an `await` catches a rejected promise just like a thrown synchronous error, so the `catch` block runs and prints `caught: boom`.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between `Promise.all` and `Promise.allSettled`?

options.text: `Promise.all` rejects as soon as any input promise rejects; `Promise.allSettled` always resolves with each promise's outcome
`Promise.allSettled` runs promises sequentially; `Promise.all` runs them in parallel
They behave identically but `allSettled` is deprecated
`Promise.all` only accepts a single promise, not an array

questions.explanation: `Promise.all` fails fast: the first rejection short-circuits the whole call. `Promise.allSettled` waits for every promise and reports each as `{ status: "fulfilled", value }` or `{ status: "rejected", reason }`, never rejecting itself.

questions.prompt:
What is printed?

```js
Promise.resolve(1)
  .then((v) => v + 1)
  .then((v) => console.log(v));
console.log("sync");
```
questions.explanation: Both `.then` callbacks are scheduled as microtasks, which only run after the current synchronous code finishes. `console.log("sync")` runs first, then the chained `.then` handlers produce `2`.
